page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-128GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 16 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng testing, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression, placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression perform in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, Passmark metrics, and Redis SET operations fall within the average range, reflecting the shared CPU allocation model under multi-threaded workloads.

The shared CPU allocation model offers a cost-effective alternative for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated CPU performance. With a high memory density of 128.0 GB, this server is well-suited for memory-optimized tasks, including caching layers, large-scale data processing, and memory-heavy web serving. It is also appropriate for development environments, software compilation, and database operations that benefit from high memory capacity and strong single-threaded execution.
